clue.text: Fruit is dear — women led off …

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment, like dear or darling

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone admires a fruit while a group of women set off, the ellipsis carrying the sentence into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram; 'led off' reads like the women walking away, and the ellipsis links this clue's surface to the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeydew melon is a pale-fleshed sweet variety of melon, a fruit.

clue.text: Making pie, I'd most bananas made best use of

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A baker says making a pie with bananas was making the most of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but means mad, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To optimise something is to get the most effective result from it.

clue.text: Spirit found in a set sweet hospital provides

indicators.note: provides says the letters are supplied from within the words next to it

explanation.surface: A caring atmosphere found in a hospital that is kind and well run.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'sweET HOSpital'; a set here is a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or outlook shared by a group or community.

clue.text: Sees fruit cooked instead?

definitions.meaning: to see someone can mean to go out with them romantically
the sweet brown fruit of the palm tree

explanation.surface: A question about fruit being cooked as an alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked instead?' is a bonus hint: STEAD, the end of 'instead', when cooked (anagrammed) gives the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing someone romantically means going on outings with them; the palm fruit is the second sense.

clue.text: Dying to be thin, I grew monstrously

indicators.note: monstrously suggests a grotesque distortion, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to be slim grew in a monstrous way.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that wither shrivel and die, so withering means fading away.

clue.text: Cryptic crossword started after setter drinks gin served up at lunchtime

indicators.note: after means the crossword letter follows the other pieces
served up, in a down clue, means the combined letters are read from bottom to top
drinks means the setter word takes the gin inside it

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
taken as written
lunchtime is one o'clock, and one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: started says only the opening letter of crossword is used

explanation.surface: The setter starts a crossword after downing a lunchtime gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses the setter-with-gin piece, as this is a down clue. Lunchtime is one o'clock, giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic and puzzling both describe something mysterious or hard to make out.

clue.text: One who has oranges with "navels", eaten regularly for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone who owns navel oranges eats them every day as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, the one holding it.

clue.text: Parish people annoyed about Liberal toady

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around the Liberal abbreviation
annoyed means stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, a British political party

explanation.surface: Villagers get cross about a Liberal crawler in their midst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoyed' is the anagram signal and 'about' puts the scrambled villagers around the Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple-polisher is an American term for a sycophant who seeks favour by flattery.

clue.text: What some brides wear, fixed on large bosoms

indicators.note: fixed can mean rigged or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky wedding remark about what is pinned to an ample bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed on' looks like fastened to, but 'fixed' is the anagram signal for ON LARGE BOSOMS.
explanation.definitionFit: White citrus flowers are traditionally worn by brides in wreaths and bouquets.

clue.text: … to shop around, with little time for critical remark

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: the women go shopping, and someone makes a cutting comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the surface to 1-across; 'around' is the anagram signal, not a direction for shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a casual, sniping criticism, a cheap remark aimed at someone.

clue.text: Hotel in Canning person finds less gross

indicators.note: in says the hotel letter goes inside the word for the canning worker

parts.note: a tinner is someone who works putting food into tins, that is canning
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A worker at a hotel in the town of Canning finds things less disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canning' looks like a place name, but it means the act of putting food in cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean fat or bulky, so being slimmer means being less gross.

clue.text: Small girl nearly returned fruit

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: nearly says the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Emily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A little girl, nearly home again, brings back some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims EMILY to EMIL; S plus EMIL, all reversed by 'returned', gives LIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Limes are small green citrus fruits.

clue.text: Second XI has one chap that's good for an evening out

parts.note: a cricket or football side of eleven players is a team, written XI
one is the Roman numeral I
Ron is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A member of the second eleven says he's good company for a night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' reads as a social night, but it means making creased cloth even.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing appliance smooths creases, so it is useful for making fabric flat and even.

clue.text: Bother reaching last of tomato sauce

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, a bother

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up at reaching the end of the tomato sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil, pine-nut and cheese sauce served with pasta.

clue.text: Order is one half-quince? Respect!

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour
a means one

indicators.note: half here says the front three letters of the fruit word are lost, leaving the back half

explanation.surface: Someone ordering half a quince demands respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a show of deep respect, such as a bow or curtsey.

clue.text: Like PDFs, can be speedily run off first?

indicators.note: off first says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to sprint is to run at full speed
able means capable of, so it stands for can be

explanation.surface: A question about whether PDF files can be printed out quickly before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run off' looks like printing, but 'off first' removes the S from SPRINT.
explanation.definitionFit: PDF documents are designed to be sent to a printer, so they are fit for printing.

clue.text: Like 19 and 23, eating it with 4 is uncivilised

indicators.note: eating means the outer word takes the rest inside it

parts.note: the numbers nineteen and twenty-three are both prime, divisible only by themselves and one
taken as written
four is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Cross-references to other clues suggest something rough and uncivilised.
explanation.walkthrough: '19 and 23' look like clue references, but they are just numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means at an early stage of development, crude or uncultured.

clue.text: It'd be a big surprise, dropping this stunning woman

definitions.text: It'd be a big surprise, dropping this
definitions.meaning: to drop one is to announce shocking news
a glamorous, very attractive woman, as in a blonde one

explanation.surface: It would be a shock to see a beautiful woman fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a devastating piece of news and a strikingly attractive woman.

clue.text: The answer when fish swallows snake? Making a run for it

indicators.note: swallows means the fish word takes the snake word inside it

parts.note: ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family
the adder is Britain's only venomous snake

explanation.surface: A riddle about a fish gulping a snake, then a phrase about escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a run' is not fleeing but a ladder, a vertical split in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights ladder when a line of stitches unravels, which is called a run in American English.

clue.text: Arrived and left in a biplane

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone flew in and departed in an old two-winged aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sopwith Camel was a British First World War fighter biplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camel was a famous single-seat fighter aircraft with two sets of wings.

clue.text: Function without garden implements — hard thing for 8 part 2 to accomplish?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the function word goes around the rest

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
hoes are garden tools for weeding
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Something working without its garden tools, and a hard task for someone to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 8 part 2 is POLISHER, the second word of 8-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffing footwear to a gleam is exactly a job a polisher would carry out.

clue.text: Waste a bit of fruit loaf, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are muddled
a bit of takes just the opening letter of fruit

explanation.surface: Throwing away a slice of fruit loaf is a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal originally meant refuse or scraps, and still names discarded parts or rubbish.

clue.text: One rousing game sees opener dismissed for 8 part 1? If so, it could be Jonathan

indicators.note: opener dismissed means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a beater drives game birds out of cover for shooters

explanation.surface: A cricket-flavoured scene of an opening batsman out, mixed with game shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 part 1 is APPLE (from 8-down): an eater is an apple for eating raw, and Jonathan is such a variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan is a dessert apple variety, so it is one eaten raw rather than cooked.

clue.text: Jars of fruit

definitions.meaning: to jar is to grate harshly, and so do coarse files or scraping noises
informal British short form for raspberries

explanation.surface: Containers of preserved fruit, as on a pantry shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jars' looks like a noun for containers but is a verb meaning grates on the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Jars as grates harshly is a verb sense; the fruit sense is a casual short form of raspberries.

clue.text: Farm producing a batch of Andorran cherries

indicators.note: batch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farm in Andorra produces a crop of cherries.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'producing'; that word is only a link, so the definition is 'Farm' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle or horses.

clue.text: Address for Turkish man, if prime of figs need re-ordering

indicators.note: re-ordering says the letters gathered here are put in a new sequence
prime of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Turkish man asks whether the best figs need sorting.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-ordering' shuffles IF, F (the first of figs) and NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a Turkish title of respect for an educated man, used like sir.

clue.text: One setter's into fruit!

indicators.note: the 's stands for is, and with the in of into says the pieces are put inside the container

parts.note: into is read as in plus to, and its to part is the container word
an means one, as in an apple
gel is something that sets, as hair gel sets a style

explanation.surface: The setter exclaims that they are keen on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'into' as 'in TO': the setter's pieces are in the word TO. 'setter' is not the compiler but something that sets, like hair gel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo.

clue.text: A number down fruit squash, ultimately getting sick

parts.note: feeling down means feeling blue
a berry is a small fruit

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone, low after eating squashed fruit, ends up feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song: Blueberry Hill was a hit for Fats Domino.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and this one is a classic 1950s hit.
